item.title: Study reveals distinct patterns across single-, multi-, and mass homicides
item.description: An updated analysis of U.S. homicide data has found that intimate partner violence (IPV) often precipitates mass homicide and is also frequently associated with multi-victim and single-victim deaths. The study categorizes homicides into single-victim, multi-victim (2–3 victims) and mass (4 or more victims, excluding the perpetrator) fatalities, revealing distinct demographics and circumstances. The findings of the study published in Annals of Epidemiology, can help inform the development of tailored strategies to prevent homicide. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Each extra hour of prolonged sitting linked to 9% higher cancer death risk
item.description: Sitting for long, uninterrupted stretches may carry greater health risks than sitting the same amount of time in shorter bouts. Researchers found that each extra hour of prolonged sedentary behavior was associated with a 9% higher risk of cancer death. Breaking up sitting with movement showed the opposite pattern, while replacing an hour of prolonged sitting with light activity was linked to a 12% lower risk. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
